title: Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd - 544252 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 FY27: PAT up 18% YoY to INR757 crore, AUM at INR1.58 lakh crore growing 25%, with management flagging ~25 bps NIM compression ahead.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed AUM crossing INR1.5 lakh crore, disbursements up 25% YoY to INR19,900 crore, and stable asset quality (GNPA 29 bps, NNPA 12 bps). Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: AUM growth 22% YoY (vs 20% in Q1); home loans are 53.9% of AUM. GNPA 36 bps (up from 34 bps); NNPA 16 bps (up 1 bp).

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM growth 26% YoY. GNPA down 1 bp QoQ to 61 bps; NNPA down 4 bps to 21 bps.

segments.name: Loan against rental/LRD
segments.commentary: AUM growth 39% YoY (vs 41% in Q1). GNPA 2 bps, due to one retail account moving from Stage 2 to NPA; NNPA 1 bp. Management says excluding this, quality remains strong.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF)
segments.commentary: AUM growth 13% YoY and the book declined QoQ on higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements. GNPA flat at 12 bps; NNPA down 3 bps. Management targets 15-17% of portfolio.

segments.name: Sambhav (affordable housing)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate crossed INR500 crore; now 16% of home loan originations by value (vs 14% in Q1). ATS about INR28 lakh; 65% of customers have bureau score above 750; 66% salaried.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 21-23% for FY27 kept unchanged; AUM is currently growing 25%, but management flagged a possible slowdown to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags the repo hike.
NIM compression of about 25 bps for the year reiterated; management said a further 1-2 bps hit is possible if acquisition pricing pressure is severe.
ROA guidance of 2.1-2.3% retained; current 2.2%, with possibly 2-3 bps of additional compression in a stress case.
Management expects the repo hike to flow through about 80-82% to cost of funds and portfolio yields. Under a 75 bps hike scenario, cost of funds could rise about 61-62 bps to exit FY27.
Sambhav targeted at about 20% of home loan mix by year-end and around 30% over 3-4 years; monthly disbursement target of INR600 crore by year-end.
Opex to NTI, targeted to fall about 1% a year, may stay flat next year if insurance commission cuts are implemented. Salary costs to keep rising YoY for about four more quarters.
capex_capacity: Sambhav runs a centralised underwriting model with regionalised operations centres, and is scaling via B2C, B2B and D2C channels.
Management is recalibrating the mix toward non-prime, LAP and construction finance if prime acquisition pricing stays weak.
demand_pricing: Portfolio yield fell to 8.8%; incremental loan yield around 8.1% in both Q1 and Q2. Management expects pass-through of the repo hike to the portfolio in line with cost of funds.

Floating-rate assets: 25-30% linked to repo; internal FRR book (about 54% of assets, or 60-62% of floating assets) linked to PLR. PLR raised 15 bps effective 16 October 2026; new acquisition pricing expected to rise about 15-20 bps.
Bank MCLR hikes by leading public sector banks and an early 15-20 bps move by one or two banks were cited; a clearer picture expected around 24-25 October.
Management said prime pricing competition from PSU and private banks is an ongoing feature; if acquisition pricing lags, prime attrition may rise and the company will lean on non-prime growth.

Insurance commission regulation draft: management estimated 10-11% of PBT comes from cross-sell income; about 4-5% can be offset, leaving 6-7% of PBT at risk. Sambhav fees and prime efficiencies may offset part of this, mainly on a longer-term basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

risks_watch: Acquisition pricing pass-through by banks after the repo hike, due around 24-25 October; a lag could increase prime attrition and cut AUM growth from 25% toward 22-23%.
Insurance commission regulation: a 6-7% PBT impact is possible if the draft guidelines stand, which would push opex to NTI flat next year.
Developer finance book: a QoQ decline and 13% YoY growth; watch whether disbursements recover in Q3-Q4 as management expects.
Rising salary costs (19% YoY in Q2) as Sambhav and senior hires build out; management expects elevated costs for 1.5-2 years.
Home loan GNPA rose to 36 bps from 34 bps; watch for further upward movement, and whether the single LRD slippage stays isolated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and profitability. Cautious and non-committal on margins and acquisition pricing, which management said is still unclear after the repo hike, and it declined to revise guidance.
key_quotes: Overall good quarter across growth, asset quality, and profitability.

We are yet to see the impact in the market because acquisition pricing not moving can lead to a higher attrition pressure again largely on the prime housing and some extent LRD, because both of these are most price-sensitive customers.
So, largely we are an optimized balance sheet with interest rate having asset to liability floating almost completely matched.
